To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
capicua represses the expression of the dorsal follicle cell determinant mirror, and that capicua is required in follicle cells to establish the ventral limit of the eggshell appendage primordium.
Capicua represses mirror expression in the follicle cell epithelium to prevent ectopic formation of eggshell appendages along the dorso-ventral axis.
Capicua functions in the follicle cell fate decision to block mirror expression and that this repression is required to establish the ventral follicle cell boundary.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how cells in the follicle cells of the Drosophilavarium are determined to adopt different fates along the anterior-posterior and dorsoventral axes.
the mechanisms that control the formation of eggshell appendages in the Drosophilal ovary.
the mechanisms that control the pattern of cell fate determination along the dorso-ventral axis of a tissue.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Capicua is a key regulator of follicle cell fate determination in the Drosophilia ovary.

the transcriptional regulator Capicua is a repressor of mirror in follicle cells, and this repression of mirror by Capicua is necessary for the establishment of the follicle cell pattern along the dorso-ventral axis of Drosophila eggs.

the Capicua transcriptional repressor regulates the pattern of cell fates along a dorsoventral gradient by blocking the induction and/or maintenance of dorsal fates by Egfr and by anterior positional cues.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Capicua is a key factor in the follicle cell fate decision, and it is required to repress the dorsal fates in the ventral follicle cells.
capicua is required to repress the dorsal follicle cell fated genes mirror and staufen, which in turn, repress the ventral cell fate determinant, bag of marbles.
capicua is required in the ventral follicle cells to prevent mirror expression, which is required for dorsal appendage formation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dorsoventrally patterned follicle cells are generated by a combination of positive and negative regulation of the same set of determinants.
the dorsoventrally asymmetric expression of mirror is established by the combined action of the Egfr pathway in the dorsal follicle cells and the capicua pathway in the ventral follicle cells.
the transcriptional repression of a dorsal fate gene, mirror, is required to establish the ventral limit of the dorsal appendage primordium.
